latest_release.body:
Bundles uBlock Origin 1.75.4.

## What's Changed
* Firefox 159: stock parity for a driven browser by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/997
* Report the software renderer on a host that renders in software by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1006
* Read current WebSocket close arguments by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/988
* Ship release packages every user can read by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1002
* Read the spoofed user agent once by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/984
* Expose EXT_texture_norm16 on Windows WebGL2 by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1005
* Assert contexts keep separate content processes by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/991
* Accept Playwright's bypassServiceWorker in Network.setRequestInterception by @dyiapanis in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/976
* Leave the page when a humanized curve does by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/987
* Hold the startup window size through a late window-manager frame by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/973
* Bound the host GPU probe and fail loudly by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/985
* Place a proxied context where its proxy exits by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/990
* Keep the display when repairing a zoomed devicePixelRatio by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1003
* Give OffscreenCanvas no WebGL2 when webgl.enable-webgl2 is off by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1022
* Report WebGL2's value for every parameter WebGL1 shares by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1020
* Keep a routed request's header order on the wire by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/989
* humanize: leave the page straight across the edge, 3px from the last move by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1026
* Bundle a committed uBlock Origin release, not AMO's newest by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1012
* Canvas and Opus follow a claimed CPU vendor (Intel/AMD); vendor joins the fingerprint by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1024
* cpu-vendor-estimates: compute as Intel or AMD x86-64 on an ARM64 host by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1034
* driven-move-coalescing: pin the display scale and expect device pixels by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1035
* verify-fonts: check aliases per OS version, and run it on pull requests by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1036
* release: fix the Windows x86_64 build and let every target build to the end by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1038
* getter-cost-parity: fail the renderer strings only when they skip the round trip by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1039
* CI: test a tree once, and bound the getter-cost round trip at 1/10 of stock by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1042
* cpu-vendor-estimates: move its hunks to additions into the additions by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1054
* Hide the driver from stacks and callers a page reads by @coleleavitt in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1053
* CI: build pull requests with the release's command, and preflight its other targets by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1055
* Check the host-fetched WebGL limits with a switch, not a scan by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1062
* Check that humanized moves arrive at refresh ticks by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/978
* Make run builds valid CAMOU_CONFIG JSON (#1072) by @alfonsodg in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/1082
* patch-guards: check that a bare launch on Linux re

--- # Introduction Camoufox is a Firefox build for web scraping and AI agents. Every launch gets a fresh, internally consistent device identity drawn from the real-world distribution of devices, and the browser reports it from C++, so a page sees native values rather than JavaScript overrides. Playwright drives it, through an automation layer the page cannot see. | Package | Install | Docs | |---|---|---| | Python | `pip install -U "camoufox[geoip]"` | [`python/README.md`](python/README.md) | | TypeScript / Node.js | `npm install camoufox playwright-core` | [`typescript/README.md`](typescript/README.md) | | AI coding agents | | [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md#using-camoufox) | ## Quick start ```bash pip install -U "camoufox[geoip]" camoufox fetch ``` ```python from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox with Camoufox(headless=True) as browser: page = browser.new_page() page.goto("https://example.com") ``` ```python import asyncio from camoufox.async_api import AsyncCamoufox async def main(): async with AsyncCamoufox(headless=True) as browser: page = await browser.new_page() await page.goto("https://example.com") asyncio.run(main()) ``` ```javascript // npm install camoufox playwright-core && npx camoufox fetch import { Camoufox } from "camoufox"; const browser = await Camoufox({ headless: true }); const page = await browser.newPage(); await page.goto("https://example.com"); await browser.close(); ``` What you get back is a normal Playwright `Browser`. Behind a proxy, add `proxy=...` and `geoip=True` so timezone, locale, geolocation and the WebRTC IP match the exit IP. For many identities in one browser, use `NewContext()`. ## How it fits together ```mermaid flowchart TB YOU(["Your Playwright code"]) subgraph L["Launcher: python/ or typescript/"] FP["fpgen
draws a real device"] --> CO["coherence.py
rejects impossible combinations"] CO --> ID[["Identity"]] GEO["geoip
timezone, locale, WebRTC IP"] --> ID end subgraph B["Patched Firefox: browser/"] MC["MaskConfig
reads CAMOU_CONFIG"] --> API["Web APIs answered in C++
navigator, screen, WebGL,
fonts, audio, WebRTC"] SET["Per-context setters
sealed before page script"] --> API JG["Juggler
isolated world"] end PAGE(["The web page"]) YOU -- "1 launch options" --> L ID == "2 CAMOU_CONFIG + prefs" ==> MC ID -- "3 NewContext()" --> SET YOU <-- "4 Juggler protocol" --> JG API -- "native values" --> PAGE JG -. "trusted input, DOM reads;
no code in the page" .-> PAGE classDef you fill:#eef2f6,stroke:#57606a,color:#1f2328 classDef launcher fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#0969da,color:#0a3069 classDef browser fill:#fff1e5,stroke:#bc4c00,color:#4a1c00 classDef page fill:#dafbe1,stroke:#1a7f37,color:#0f3d1c class YOU you class FP,CO,ID,GEO launcher class MC,API,SET,JG browser class PAGE page style L fill:none,stroke:#0969da,stroke-dasharray:4 3,color:#0969da style B fill:none,stroke:#bc4c00,stroke-dasharray:4 3,color:#bc4c00 ``` 1. The launcher draws a device from [fpgen](https://github.com/scrapfly/fingerprint-generator) (a model of real traffic), then adds fonts, voices, a GPU and media devices seeded by that identity. `coherence.py` rejects combinations no real machine produces. 2. The identity goes to the browser as the `CAMOU_CONFIG` environment variable (keys declared in [`browser/settings/properties.json`](browser/settings/properties.json)). The patches read it through `MaskConfig` and answer from C++. 3. `NewContext()` gives one context its own identity through setters that the per-context patches add to `window`. They are sealed before page script runs. 4. Playwright talks to Juggler. Camoufox's Juggler runs its page agent in an isolated world, so the page never sees automation code. # Features Each row says where it is implemented. A **patch** is a file in [`browser/patches/`](browser/patches); **Juggler** is [`browser/additions/juggler/`](browser/additions/juggler); the **launcher** is the Python and TypeScript packages. ### Fingerprint spoofing The goal is a browser that behaves exactly like stock Firefox, except that it reports a different machine. A value is spoofed when it identifies the host machine or the network. Anything else stays as Firefox has it, because something stock Firefox never does, such as noise, is a fingerprint in its own right. | Trait | What a page sees | Why it is spoofed | Where | |---|---|---|---| | Navigator: User-Agent, platform, oscpu, hardware concurrency, language, appVersion | The drawn device's values, per launch or per context, in workers too | They name the OS and hardware directly, and every other value is checked against them | `navigator-spoofing`, `fingerprint-injection` patches | | HTTP headers: User-Agent, Accept-Language | The navigator values | Servers compare the headers with what script reports | `network-patches` patch | | Screen and window sizes, color depth, CSS media features | The drawn device's display, the same in JS and CSS | Screen size is among the most identifying values, and CSS media queries read it without script | `screen-spoofing`, `fingerprint-injection` patches | | WebGL and WebGL2: vendor, renderer, parameters, extensions, shader precision, context attributes | One GPU fpgen recorded for Firefox on that OS. Values Firefox decides rather than the GPU follow the shipped Firefox ([`webgl-browser-owned-values-follow-firefox`](ci/tribal-rules.yml)) | The renderer string names the host's GPU, and its limits must agree with it | `webgl-spoofing` patch, `webgl.py` | | WebGPU: `navigator.gpu` and its adapter | `navigator.gpu` only where Firefox on the claimed device has it: Windows and Apple Silicon Macs. The adapter is the host's only when the identity claims the host's GPU; otherwise `requestAdapter()` returns `null`, as for a blocked or software GPU | The adapter's limits and features come from the real GPU | launcher, `host_rendering.py` | | Canvas, Web Audio, Opus, VP9, relaxed-SIMD wasm and NaN bits | The claimed CPU's arithmetic. Intel and AMD implement Skia's and Opus's estimate instructions RCPPS/RSQRTPS with different tables, so on an AMD host a canvas drawn with `color-dodge`, `color-burn`, `hue`, `saturation`, `color` or `luminosity` reads back other pixels than on Intel; an ARM64 CPU differs in far more (every Web Audio node and composite operation, Opus, VP9, NaN signs, relaxed SIMD). An x86-64 build computes as Intel, AMD or ARM64. `cpu` picks one; by default it follows the GPU (an Apple GPU is ARM, an Intel iGPU or Intel Mac is Intel, a Radeon iGPU is AMD) and otherwise is x86, 81% Intel as among Firefox's x86 users | The results split by CPU, not by OS or CPU generation, so they show the host's CPU | `cpu-vendor-estimates` patch, launcher | | Audio: sample rate, output latency, max channels | The identity's values | They follow the claimed device's audio hardware | `audio-context-spoofing` patch | | Fonts: installed list, `system-ui`, CSS2 system fonts | The claimed OS's fonts, from a bundled set; see [docs/FONTS.md](docs/FONTS.md) | Installed fonts reveal the OS and the software on it | `font-list-spoofing`, `font-hijacker`, `system-ui-font-spoofing` patches | | Speech voices | The claimed OS's voices, which actually speak | The voice list is specific to each OS, and a voice that cannot speak is a tell | `voice-spoofing`, `speech-voices-spoofing` patches | | Microphones, cameras, speakers | OS-style labels and groups; see [docs/MEDIA-DEVICES.md](docs/MEDIA-DEVICES.md) | Device count and labels differ per machine and per OS | `media-device-spoofing` patch | | Media codecs (`canPlayType`, `isTypeSupported`) | Not the host's codec libraries | On Linux the answer depends on the host's installed codec libraries | `media-codec-spoofing` patch | | Timezone, locale and `Intl` | The identity's, per realm, workers included | They must agree with the IP's country | `timezone-spoofing`, `locale-spoofing` patches | | Geolocation | Coordinates from GeoIP, permission granted | They must agree with the IP | `geolocation-spoofing` patch, launcher | | WebRTC IP | ICE candidates, SDP and `getStats()` rewritten to the proxy IP | WebRTC otherwise reveals the real IP behind a proxy | `webrtc-ip-spoofing` patch | | WebRTC UDP behind a SOCKS5 proxy | STUN, TURN and peer-to-peer UDP go through the proxy's UDP relay (UDP ASSOCIATE), so the srflx candidate is the address the page's STUN server really saw; the local network gets no exception, and mDNS names stay in the browser. Without a relay, no UDP leaves the host and the srflx carries the proxy IP. Only a page's own loopback connection stays direct | Stock Firefox on the exit machine gathers a real srflx and connects peer to peer | `webrtc-socks5-udp` patch | | Touchscreen | A touchscreen laptop, not a phone | Touch points and pointer media must agree with the claimed device | `touchscreen-fingerprint-spoofing`, `force-default-pointer` patches | Left as stock Firefox has it, on purpose: | Trait | What a page sees | Why it is not spoofed | |---|---|---| | Canvas pixels | What the GPU and fonts produce. As in stock Firefox, each context's PNG exports (`toDataURL`, `toBlob`) carry a per-session `deBG` chunk; the pixels themselves are untouched. On the host's OS the identity claims the host's GPU, so the pixels agree with it; on another OS readback returns random data, as `privacy.resistFingerprinting` does in LibreWolf ([the canvas on another OS](python/README.md#the-canvas-on-another-os)) | Stock Firefox does not perturb pixels in its default configuration, so noise would only mark the browser as a spoofer ([`canvas-is-not-noised`](ci/tribal-rules.yml)) | | Text widths | What the font really measures | The same font on the same OS measures the same everywhere; widths no real machine produces are a fingerprint ([`no-glyph-spacing-noise`](ci/tribal-rules.yml)) | | Audio render (`OfflineAudioContext`, `AnalyserNode`) | What the host CPU computes, the same in every context and every launch | Stock Firefox renders one value per CPU architecture, whatever the OS, sound card or sample rate, so a noised value is one no real machine produces ([`audio-is-not-noised`](ci/tribal-rules.yml)) | Each context of one browser can carry its own identity: [docs/per-context-patches.md](docs/per-context-patches.md). ### Canvas Canvas and WebGL pixels come from the real OS, driver and GPU, whatever the identity claims. The launcher chooses the canvas behaviour from two facts: does the identity claim the host's OS, and does the host render on a GPU? | | Identity on the host's OS | Identity on another OS | |---|---|---| | **GPU rendering** | 🟢 Most stealthy
    ✅ No canvas noise: looks like stock Firefox
    ✅ The claimed GPU is the host's, so the pixels agree with it
    ⛔ Every identity on this machine claims the same GPU, so there is less fingerprint diversity | 🟡 Less stealthy
    ✅ Readback is random, so the real OS does not show
    ✅ A GPU is drawn per identity, so identities differ
    ⛔ Canvas noise: looks like LibreWolf, Tor Browser or Mullvad Browser, which are rarer than stock Firefox | | **Software rendering**
(no working GPU driver, as on most servers) | 🟡 Less stealthy
    ✅ No canvas noise: looks like stock Firefox
    ✅ Claims the software renderer (`llvmpipe` on Linux), so the pixels agree with it
    ⛔ Reads as a server or a broken driver, and every identity on this machine claims the same renderer | 🟡 Less stealthy
    ✅ Readback is random, so the real OS does not show
    ✅ A GPU is drawn per identity, so identities differ
    ⛔ Canvas noise: looks like LibreWolf, Tor Browser or Mullvad Browser, which are rarer than stock Firefox | A software-rendering host never claims a GPU. Firefox reads the name and the pixels from one GL context, so a GPU name over software pixels never happens on a real machine: with a broken GPU driver, Firefox reports `llvmpipe` too. To report a GPU, render on one with `headless="virtual-gpu"`. That is the default. These options override it: | Override | Result | |---|---| | `canvas_noise=False` on another OS | 🔴 Stock Firefox, but the pixels show the real OS | | `canvas_noise=True` on the host's OS | 🟡 Looks like LibreWolf with no need to | | `webgl_config` naming a GPU other than the host's | 🟡 Canvas noise is turned on, as on another OS; with `canvas_noise=False`, 🔴 WebGL reports one GPU while the pixels come from another | Noise is set per browser, not per context. Without it, every `NewContext()` claims the host's OS. Details are in [the canvas on another OS](python/README.md#the-canvas-on-another-os). ### Hiding automation | What | Where | |---|---| | Playwright's `evaluate`, selectors and init scripts run in an isolated world the page cannot see | Juggler | | `navigator.webdriver` is `false` | `playwright/1-leak-fixes` patch | | `select_option`, `fill` on date and colour inputs, and `set_input_files` fire trusted events | `trusted-automation-events` patch | | `fill` and `keyboard.insert_text` paste the text as a person does: the paste shortcut and Firefox's own paste, without the system clipboard | Juggler | | Screenshots leave the page's DOM alone (no caret-hiding style writes) | Launcher | | Mouse moves coalesce per frame as a real mouse's do, spaced as a 125 Hz mouse's | Juggler, `input-coalescing-parity` patch | | A drag fires `drag` at its source with each motion, as GTK does | Juggler, `drag-source-events` patch | | Driver calls define no interfaces on the page's window | `isolated-world-global-order` patch | | A SOCKS5 proxy with a username and password works, for the launch and per context: the launcher hands the credentials to Juggler, which Playwright alone refuses | Launcher, Juggler | | Headless reports a fine pointer, like a desktop | `force-default-pointer` patch | | `mouse.wheel()` turns notches, as a physical wheel does: 100 px is one notch, each its own event with a native tick | Juggler, `wheel-native-ticks` patch | | A press's click count is the identity's OS's, counted from the presses before it; Playwright's `click_count` is ignored. A held key repeats with that OS's delay and interval | Juggler | | Juggler's debugger leaves no side effects content can observe | `debugger-invisible-to-content` patch | | A stack the page captures while a driver call runs its code (`focus`, `dispatch_event`, an `mw:` evaluate) holds only the page's frames, never Juggler's, the isolated world's or the code the `mw:` evaluate compiled; a page function's `caller` is never driver code | Juggler, `debugger-invisible-to-content` patch | | Code an `mw:` evaluate runs is named after the document, as an inline script is, never `debugger eval code` | Juggler, `debugger-invisible-to-content` patch | | Per-context fingerprint setters are gone before page script runs | `window-setter-seal` patch | | Popup blocker on, as in stock Firefox | `popup-blocker-parity` patch | | On X11, a pointer-locked window partly off the top or left of the screen keeps running (stock Firefox can crash: the X server refuses the cursor barrier and GDK aborts) | `pointer-lock-offscreen` patch | | Content-accessible chrome files match stock Firefox | `contentaccessible-parity` patch | | Viewports never enter Responsive Design Mode; containers show no automation label | Juggler | ### Automation | Feature | How to use it | Where | |---|---|---| | Human input: none in the browser. Some WAFs test SpiderMonkey engine > behaviour, which no amount of spoofing turns into Chromium. # How Camoufox compares | | JavaScript injection | CDP-based (Chromium) | Camoufox | |---|---|---|---| | Where values are spoofed | Page-world overrides | Page-world overrides or flags | Browser C++ | | `toString()`, property descriptors | Show the override | Show the override | Native | | Workers and iframes | Often missed | Often missed | Same value everywhere | | Headers agree with navigator | Only if set separately | Only if set separately | Always | | Automation code in the page | Yes | Yes (bindings, `navigator.webdriver`) | No: isolated world | | Identity source | Hand-picked or random | Hand-picked or random | fpgen's real-world distribution, coherence-checked | Playwright drives Chromium over CDP but Firefox over Juggler, a protocol that is a separate module inside Firefox. That makes it possible to give Juggler its own copy of the page: Playwright reads and edits that copy, and the real page never sees a getter fire or a listener appear. Input goes through Firefox's own input handlers, so it is handled as a user's would be. Camoufox can still be detected. Thousands of values must agree with each other, and anti-bot vendors look for the one that does not. File a [detection report](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/issues/new?template=camoufox-detected.md) when you find one. ## Human input The browser does not humanize input. Each Playwright input call reaches the page as one event of the shape a real device gives stock Firefox: a `mouse.move` is one move, a click is a press and a release, `mouse.wheel(dx, dy)` is one wheel event in whole notches (Linux and Windows: 100 px a notch, carried in that one event as a fast spin of a notched wheel can be; macOS: one event of 16 px lines), and `fill()` is Firefox's own paste. The browser adds no timing, paths, pacing or randomness of its own, so how human the input looks is up to the driver: send the moves, notches and keys a person would, at a person's times ([docs/input-dispatch.md](docs/input-dispatch.md) has each event's shape per OS). The `humanize` option picks an engine per channel, run in your own process: ```python from camoufox.humanize import myuri, raw Camoufox(humanize=True) # myuri() on every channel Camoufox(humanize={"scroll": raw(), "seed": 1234}) Camoufox(humanize={"settings": {"mouse": {"speed_factor": 2}, "typing": {"wpm": 90}}}) ``` ![A Linux identity with humanize on: myuri fills a form, types two lines, clicks buttons and scrolls to one 1800 px down](browser/assets/humanize.gif) A Linux identity with `humanize={"seed": 7}`, recorded at real speed. The red trail and the rings are drawn by the page from the mouse events it received. - `myuri()` is [myuri](https://github.com/JWriter20/Myuri)'s smart actions, fitted to recordings of people on each OS and drawn for the launch identity's OS: the path, the press, the typing and the wheel turns, and the decisions around a click (scroll the element into view, choose the point, check that the press lands, try again when it does not). Both packages depend on it, pinned to the release they were tested with. - `cursory()` is another name for `myuri()`: myuri runs cursory's paths. - `raw()` is Playwright as it is. - A channel a dict leaves out is `myuri()`. `humanize=None` or `False`, the default, is `raw()` everywhere. - `settings` are [myuri's settings](https://github.com/JWriter20/Myuri#settings): mouse, scroll and typing speed, overshoot, typing mistakes and pauses. Pass any subset; the rest keep myuri's defaults, and an unknown key raises `ValueError` before launch. The `seed` draws one person around them, each speed within ±`variation` (0.2) of the value set; `{"variation": 0}` plays them exactly. The engine decides when each event happens; the browser decides what each event looks like for the identity's OS ([docs/humanize.md](docs/humanize.md)). ### Replacing a part: `myuri(part=fn)` Each piece of myuri is a part you can replace with a function of yours, in your own process (Python below; TypeScript in [its README](typescript/README.md#replacing-a-part)). The rest stay myuri's, so a scroll of your own still serves myuri's clicks, and your move still ends where myuri presses. ```python import asyncio from camoufox.async_api import AsyncCamoufox from camoufox.humanize import myuri async def my_move(page, x, y, *, default, rng, play): await asyncio.sleep(0.1 + 0.2 * rng()) # a pause to look, then myuri's path await default() async def my_into_view(page, locator, *, default, rng, play): await locator.scroll_into_view_if_needed() # Playwright's own scroll # or: await default() for myuri's wheel turns async with AsyncCamoufox(humanize={ "mouse": myuri(move=my_move), "scroll": myuri(into_view=my_into_view), "settings": {"typing": {"wpm": 70}}, "seed": 1234, }) as browser: page = await browser.new_page() await page.set_content('') await page.locator("#submit").click() # my_into_view, then myuri's click after my pause ``` | Channel | Part | Called as | myuri's part | |---|---|---|---| | `mouse` | `move` | `fn(page, x, y, ...)` | a path from the cursor to (x, y) | | | `press` | `fn(page, button, click_count, ...)` | the dwell, then each press and its hold | | | `point` | `fn(page, box, attempt, ...)`, returns `(x, y)` | where in the element's visible box to aim; `attempt` counts the misses | | | `reaches` | `fn(page, locator, x, y, pressing, ...)`, returns `None` or why it misses | whether a press at (x, y) lands on the element: not covered, enabled | | `scroll` | `into_view` | `fn(page, locator, ...)` | wheel turns until the element is in view, waiting for each scroll to land | | | `wheel` | `fn(page, dx, dy, ...)` | one scroll split into wheel notches | | `keyboard` | `type` | `fn(page, text, ...)` | keys at a person's rhythm, with the mistakes they make | | | `key` | `fn(page, key, ...)` | one key or chord (`"Enter"`, `"Control+a"`) | Every part is also called with `default`, `rng` and `play`, as keywords: - `default(*args)` runs myuri's part, with the same arguments when given none. A part that only adjusts myuri wraps it. - `rng()` returns a float in [0, 1) from the humanize seed's stream: one stream per browser, the same numbers in Python and TypeScript. - `play(steps)` dispatches steps at their times, in ms from the start of the call: `("move", x, y, t)`, `("down" | "up", button, t)`, `("wheel", dx, dy, t)` (one wheel event each), `("key", key, "down" | "up", t)`, `("text", text, t)` (pasted, as `keyboard.insert_text` is). It waits until each step is due on a monotonic clock rather than sleeping between steps, so a slow round trip delays one step and never adds up. Bad steps raise `ValueError` before anything is sent. - Playwright calls inside a part are Playwright's own: `page.mouse.move` in a move part moves the mouse once. - With the sync API a part is a plain function, and `default` and `play` return their result; with the async API they return awaitables, and the part may be `async`. Exceptions reach the caller unchanged. What each channel drives: | Channel | For | |---|---| | `mouse` | `Mouse.move`/`click`/`dblclick`; `click`, `dblclick`, `hover`, `check`, `uncheck` on a `Page`, `Frame` or `Locator`, and the click that focuses a field before `fill` | | `keyboard` | `Keyboard.type`/`press`; `fill`, `type`, `press` on a `Page`, `Frame` or `Locator`, and `Locator.press_sequentially` | | `scroll` | `Mouse.wheel`, `Locator.scroll_into_view_if_needed`, and bringing an element into view before a pointer action, fill or typing | - A click that never reaches its element raises Playwright's `TimeoutError` at the call's timeout, naming what covers the point. `trial=True` goes to Playwright alone, and `force=True` skips the reach check. - `ElementHandle` methods, `tap`, `drag_and_drop` and `drag_to` are Playwright's own. - The wrappers belong to the browser `Camoufox()` launched: other browsers in the same process are untouched. For a browser from `connect()`, launch it without humanize and call `camoufox.humanize.attach(browser, humanize, os)` with its identity's OS. Over a network each event is a round trip, so the launcher warns (`humanize_remote`). `launch_server()` refuses any engine but `raw()`. # Building the browser This repository is not the Firefox source. It fetches Firefox, copies in [`browser/additions/`](browser/additions), applies [`browser/patches/`](browser/patches) and builds. Install `ccache`. Every build is optimized as stock Firefox's releases are, with Mozilla's PGO profile for the same Firefox and cross-language LTO, and ccache cannot cache the LTO link, so an incremental build still relinks libxul. To build and package several targets in one go: ```bash python3 multibuild.py --target linux windows macos --arch x86_64 arm64 ``` | `multibuild.py` flag | Values | |---|---| | `--target` | `linux`, `windows`, `macos` (one or more) | | `--arch` | `x86_64`, `arm64`, `i686` (one or more; `i686` builds Windows only) | | `--bootstrap` | Bootstrap the build system first | | `--clean` | Clean the build directory first | | `--preflight` | Check that each target builds without building it: configure, the export tiers, and every patched source file (minutes, not hours) | Artifacts are written to `browser/dist/`. ### With Docker ```bash cd browser docker build -t camoufox-builder . docker run -v "$(pwd)/dist:/app/dist" camoufox-builder --target linux --arch x86_64 docker run -v "$(pwd)/dist:/app/dist" camoufox-builder --target windows --arch x86_64 ``` The container takes the `multibuild.py` flags.
